summary.name: MiniClaw
summary.one_liner: MiniClaw is an OpenClaw plugin ecosystem for building a persistent AI assistant with a personality, memory, and skills, which the page says runs locally on macOS.
use_cases: Run an autonomous coding agent that works tickets from a kanban board
Triage and draft replies to Gmail with an agent
Schedule and publish Substack posts automatically
Back up and restore an AI assistant's memory and identity files
Add Stripe or Square payments to an agent workflow
Give an AI agent a personal knowledge base and working memory
summary.what_it_does: MiniClaw is a set of 26 plugins for OpenClaw that add task management, long-term memory, email, publishing, payments, scheduling, and other capabilities missing from stock OpenClaw. A kanban board enforces a state machine (Backlog, In Progress, In Review, Shipped) with gates requiring a problem statement, plans, and acceptance criteria before work moves forward. A dispatch loop reportedly checks the board every 15 minutes and runs agent cycles on ready tickets. Plugins cover a SQLite and vector knowledge base, context window management, nightly self-review, identity snapshots, Gmail via OAuth2, Reddit, SEO tooling, and Stripe, Square, and Turso-backed booking. The page also describes a pre-configured Mac Mini product called AM, sold with hardware, and a paid human support service.
notable: 26 plugins for OpenClaw covering memory, kanban, email, publishing, payments, and backups
Kanban board with enforced gates before tickets can move to In Progress or Shipped
Local storage of agent personality, memory, and files in a plain folder, with the model provider swappable
Listed in awesome-mac under AI Tools as open source
caveats: Page describes a paid 'Live Support' session at $50 per 30-minute block, and a hardware product (Mac Mini) shipped pre-installed; the price of the software itself is not stated
Requires macOS 13 or later per the page
Some plugins depend on third-party services (Gmail, Stripe, Square, Reddit, Google Gemini, Telegram) and on API bills for the underlying models; the page mentions server costs and API bills
